contract.notes: Pins the JWKS/RS256 access-token validator's five T9 cases. Each case is executed by the Go, TypeScript, and Python loader tests against a real local JWKS HTTP server and real RSA keys generated in-test; no static secrets are committed. The fixture is a nested table (loaded by tests directly, not by the generic runner) because the cases need a live key server and real signatures.

defaults.unknown_kid_refresh: one bounded refresh per kid, then cooldown
defaults.audience_check: exact match against the route-derived audience

cases.name: alg-none-rejected
cases.scenario: token header alg is none and the signature is empty

cases.name: hs256-rejected
cases.scenario: token is signed HS256 using the RSA public key bytes as the HMAC secret

cases.name: unknown-kid-triggers-one-refresh
cases.scenario: token kid is absent from the bounded cache and is published by the server after the first fetch

cases.name: unknown-kid-refresh-is-bounded
cases.scenario: a second token with a still-unknown kid arrives inside the refresh cooldown

cases.name: expired-key-refresh
cases.scenario: the cached key entry has expired and the server has rotated to a new key for the same kid

cases.name: issuer-mismatch-rejected
cases.scenario: a correctly signed token whose iss is not the configured issuer

cases.name: audience-mismatch-rejected
cases.scenario: a correctly signed, correctly issued token whose aud is not the route-derived audience

cases.name: expired-token-rejected
cases.scenario: a correctly signed token whose exp is in the past
